title: On the effective sharp stability of the Faber-Krahn inequality
summary: We prove the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality with a computable dimensional constant, resolving a problem posed by Brasco and De Philippis~\cite[Open Problem~2]{brasco2017spectral}. In contrast with the known proof of the sharp estimate, our argument avoids indirect compactness arguments and selection principles. It runs through a new level-set proof of the Saint--Venant inequality, using that the torsional deficit controls both the average isoperimetric deficit and the oscillation of the gradient magnitude along the boundaries of level sets.
